This name is highly regarded in both traditional and contemporary Indian society.

This connection echoes the spiritual potential within each individual, suggesting that everyone has the ability to create their own reality through the power of their thoughts and the wisdom of their mind. The name serves as a constant reminder to live with a clear and focused mind, embodying the wisdom and intelligence of the universe itself.

historical_references.reference: Manvantara is a Hindu concept referring to a cosmic cycle or period in which the universe is created and destroyed. Each Manvantara is presided over by a Manavas or Manu, a law-giver and the first human of that period. Manu is also considered to be the creator of the human race during his Manvantara. The current Manvantara is believed to be the Vaivasvata Manvantara, which began around 3102 BCE and will last for 311,040,000 years.
historical_references.context: Cosmic cycle or period presided over by a Manu

historical_references.reference: Manu is also known as the author of the 'Manusmriti', one of the most ancient and authoritative texts in Hinduism. The Manusmriti provides a systematic and prescriptive guidance on law, ethics, social order, and personal behavior for the Hindu society. It is considered a fundamental text in the Hindu law and culture. The exact origin and time of writing of the Manusmriti is uncertain, but it is traditionally believed to have been composed around 2000 BCE.
historical_references.context: Author of a foundational text in Hinduism
